subject: Audit log exportability, PII in logs, and subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Alicia Vargas <alicia.vargas@mediacorp.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@mediacorp.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Audit logs - exportability, PII fields, and subprocessor proof

Hi Tessa,

We're working through our DPA exhibit and have a few focused questions from our Data Protection team about audit logs. Can you confirm the following so we can close this section in our review?

1) Do Redwood audit logs ever include PII (e.g., email addresses, user names) in the logged fields by default or only when present in request payloads? If PII can appear, which fields are typical?

2) Exportability: can Redwood produce on-demand exports of audit logs for customers? If yes, what formats and what protections are available (redaction, encryption, KMS options, transfer channels)?

3) Retention controls: what retention windows are configurable for audit logs per account? Is extended retention (>=180 days) available as a contract option?

4) Subprocessors: who processes or stores raw audit logs on Redwood's behalf (company names and processing locations)? We need a short list and locations (US/EU) and SOC2 status for each.

5) Will audit log exports ever leave the customer-designated region by default (during processing or for analysis)?

We're aiming to finalize the DPA exhibit by next week. If you have any example artifacts (retention matrix, keyflow diagram, subprocessors registry, SOC2 access), please include them.

Thanks,
Alicia Vargas
Data Protection Lead
MediaCorp

Attachments: sample-audit-schema.csv (we can provide if helpful)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Vargas <alicia.vargas@mediacorp.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Audit logs - exportability, PII fields, and subprocessor proof

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below plus attachments (retention matrix + KMS flow). I'll follow up with a short call invite to walk through the carve-outs.

1) PII in logs
- By default our structured audit logs capture metadata: request timestamp, model id, route, token counts, request_id, client IP (hashed) and an account-level user_id if provided by the customer.
- PII may appear only if present in the request payload and the customer chooses to persist request payloads for debugging; payload persistence is off by default for hosted accounts.
- Typical fields that could contain PII: request_payload (free text), user_email (if a customer supplies it as user_id), and any customer-provided identifiers.

2) Exportability
- Yes — we provide on-demand exports. Options: CSV/NDJSON exports or a time-bounded redacted export. Exports are delivered to a customer-owned S3 bucket or a secure HTTPS endpoint.
- Encryption: exports are encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest. For Hosted customers we use Redwood-managed encryption; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS (CMK) for export artifacts.
- Redaction: we can produce redacted exports that remove payload fields or hash user identifiers as a standard deliverable.

3) Retention controls
- Default retention: 90 days for hosted audit logs. Configurable retention windows are available for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- 180+ day retention: available as a contractual/paid option for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted accounts we can discuss a managed retention SLA but it requires technical review and cost adjustment.

4) Subprocessors
- Storage: LogStor Inc. (US, EU presence) — SOC 2 Type II.
- Analytics/query layer: QueryFlow (US) — SOC 2 Type II.
- Backup/CDN: EdgeStore (multi-region) — SOC 2 Type II.
- We will provide the formal subprocessors registry and attestation copies on request (SOC2).

5) Cross‑region processing
- We design exports and storage to honor the account region. Some transient processing (indexing) may route to a processing cluster in the nearest available region (e.g., us-east-1) but long-term retention and final export are stored in the configured region unless otherwise agreed.

Next steps / action items:
- I'm attaching the retention matrix (redwood-audit-retention-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a KMS keyflow diagram (kms-keyflow-diagram.png).
- We'll share the subprocessors registry and SOC2 report via a secure Drive link once you confirm what you need (full reports vs. summary).
- If you need a contractual clause restricting exports or requiring EU-only storage, we can scope that as an exception for Dedicated/Private; we'll need to review with legal/infra for Hosted.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Security & Privacy PM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-audit-retention-matrix-v1.xlsx (attachment stub), kms-keyflow-diagram.png (attachment stub)
From: Alicia Vargas <alicia.vargas@mediacorp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@mediacorp.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Audit logs - exportability, PII fields, and subprocessor proof

Thanks, Tessa — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- Our regulator requires 180 days of immutable audit log retention for certain regulated flows. Would Redwood be willing to commit to 180-day immutable retention as a contractual clause for those flows? We prefer region-limited retention (EU-only) for European data subjects.

- Can you confirm LogStor's processing locations for stored raw logs (are backups replicated to the US only or to EU as well)? We need explicit confirmation of data-at-rest locations for subprocessors.

- We need to see LogStor and QueryFlow SOC2 Type II summaries (not necessarily full reports). Can you provide those or a secure link?

- Finally, MediaCorp's DPA team prefers language that prevents non-consensual export of log data outside a designated region. Is Redwood open to a narrow export restriction for our account?

Appreciate it — if acceptable, please add proposed contract language or point us to the DPA appendix that would cover these exceptions.

— Alicia
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Vargas <alicia.vargas@mediacorp.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Audit logs - exportability, PII fields, and subprocessor proof

Alicia — quick update and proposed next steps.

1) 180-day retention and immutability
- We can support 180-day immutable retention as a contractual exception for Dedicated and Private deployments; this is a configuration of the storage layer and snapshot policy. For Hosted customers, we can offer a managed retention SLA but full immutability guarantees require dedicated storage and extra operational controls (we can scope as part of the deal).

2) Subprocessor locations
- LogStor: stores primary data in the customer-designated region (US or EU) and maintains geo-replicated backups by default. Backups are configurable — we can disable cross-region replication for EU-only commitments.
- QueryFlow: processing occurs in the US and EU depending on routing; we can restrict processing to specific regions for Dedicated/Private agreements.

3) SOC2 artifacts
- We'll provide SOC2 Type II summaries for LogStor and QueryFlow and a Redwood attestation. I'll share a secure Drive link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/soc2-report-2026 (shared link). If you need the full reports, we'll route through our secure evidence exchange and NDA gating.

4) Contract language / export restriction
- We are open to a narrow export restriction clause that requires Redwood to keep log data within the customer-designated region unless explicit written consent is provided. For Hosted accounts this would be an exception with associated cost and operational constraints. We'll draft proposed DPA appendix language and send it to your counsel for review.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- I'll circulate a short DPA appendix draft (export/retention carve-outs) by end of day Monday.
- If helpful, let's schedule a 30-minute call next week with infrastructure and legal to confirm the technical gating and contractual wording.

Cc'ing Neha (privacy ops) and Marcus (infra) to own the artifact delivery and contract draft.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Security & Privacy PM
Redwood Inference
